One of the biggest mistakes we see landowners make before ordering a pole barn kit: not accounting for site drainage. You can have the best kit money can buy, and if water pools where your posts go, you're setting yourself up for rot and structural issues down the road. Before you finalize your building site, walk it after a heavy rain. Where does the water go? That one step saves a lot of headaches — and we always ask our customers about it before we plan a delivery.

#PoleBarnTips #BuildRight

Here's a tip that'll save you money when buying a metal building: size up before you commit. It sounds counterintuitive, but the most common thing we hear from customers a year or two in is, "I wish I had gone a little bigger." Going from a 20x30 to a 24x36 often costs less than you'd think — and you won't outgrow it in two seasons. Our team will always give you an honest comparison so you can make the smartest call for your property and your budget. That's just how we do things.

No shade, no shelter, no flat floor. A pole barn with a simple concrete apron and some overhead clearance completely changes that scenario — and it's one of the most practical upgrades a working farm can make. A workshop bay inside your storage building isn't a luxury, it's a tool.
